newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VIERI IS THE MISSING LINK FOR ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VIERI IS THE MISSING LINK FOR ATLETICO.

text.p: Atletico Madrid's $20 million signing Christan Vieri is aiming to form a compelling atacking trio with Juninho and Spanish international "Kiko" in his new club's league title quest.
The Italian striker was officially presented to the fans and the media at Atletico's Vicente Calderon stadium on Wednesday.
He was looking happier than he had been Tuesday night when he lost his temper on arrival at Madrid's Barajas Airport after being greeted by a the barrage of TV cameras and photgraphers.
"I'm glad to becoming to Madrid," said Vieri, who has joined Atletico from Juventus.
"It's a radical move because I'm sure playing in the Spanish league will be very different from playing in Italy."
"I did not come here just for the money though. It's a big step for me but one I'm looking forward to."
Vieri, who celebrated his 24th birthday on Saturday, is seen by Atletico president Jesus Gil as the final piece in the jigsaw puzzle in his quest to regain the league title he won in 1996.
Atletico signings since the end of last season have included Brazil midfielder Juninho from England's Middlesborough and Jordi Lardin from Espanyol.
More than $51 million has already been spent on new players by Gil.
There are suggestions in the Spanish media that further players are about to be bought.
Brazilian defender Andrei Frascelli is known to be on Atletico's list of possible purchases.
Vieri is expected to lead the Atletico attack along with Francisco 'Kiko' Narvaez. Juninho is likely to play behind the pair, providing the service.
"I think that Juninho, Kiko and myself will be a good combination. They are two of the best footballers playing in Europe," said Vieri.
"It should not be difficult building up an understanding with these two guys."
Nevertheless, Vieri may be overly optimistic if he expects instant success.
Language will be a problem.
He and Juninho both speak reasonable English but hardly any Spanish while Kiko's English is negligable.
Fortunately, Atletico coach Radomir Antic speaks both English and Spanish fluently.
However, the pressure is on Antic to achieve rapid results with his new set of front line troops.
Otherwise he may become the latest in a long line of coaches to leave Atletico during the reign of the volatile Jesus Gil.
